title: Dispatch GID 1: Inventor Promises Public View of the Eidetic Stratum
summary: The Concordance Instrument will be unveiled before an audience of two hundred.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: Inventor Dr. Adrian Halden has invited the public to the Lyceum on Thursday for what he calls the first unaided view of the Eidetic Stratum. His Concordance Instrument fills much of the stage: a lamp, three lenses, and a silvered plate mounted on a frame tall enough to stand behind.

Eideticians ordinarily infer the Stratum from the differences it leaves in measurements of familiar things. Dr. Halden says a spectator facing his plate will see those differences directly. No eyepiece or training will be required. “The picture is already there,” he told our reporter. “We have only lacked a way to let a roomful of people attend to it.”

His assistant, Miss Celia Marsh, has run private trials with fewer than ten observers. She confirms that they saw images but declines to describe them before the public showing. Stage attendant Mabel Crain says the apparatus casts almost no light on the wall behind it. She has been instructed to keep the aisle clear and the exit lamps burning throughout.

Dr. Lenora Saye of the Eidetical Institute has asked Halden to postpone the demonstration until independent observers can inspect the silvered plate. He has offered her a seat in the front row instead. The Institute has neither endorsed nor prohibited the event.

The Lyceum has sold all two hundred tickets. Attendees will be asked to write down what they see before speaking to their neighbors. Halden says this will establish whether a common landscape can be verified by separate witnesses. He expects the first description to reach the newspaper before the curtain falls.
